title: IELTS General Training Reading — Full-Length Original Practice
description: Unofficial original practice: three passages, 40 questions, and 60 minutes. This is not an official IELTS test.

reading.instructions: Answer all 40 questions. Use evidence in each passage; the practice uses the teacher review workflow.

passages.title: Getting around Westbridge
passages.content:
This guide explains how residents can use the fictional Westbridge transport service. Fares and opening times below apply to the current spring timetable.

The service desk at Central Station opens at 7:30 on weekdays. A day pass allows unlimited bus and tram journeys until midnight. Children under six travel free when accompanied by a fare-paying adult. Passengers can add money to a travel card at the station or through the mobile app. The green route stops at the hospital entrance every twenty minutes. Bicycles are accepted on trains outside the morning peak. Lost property is held at the depot for fourteen days. The accessible minibus must be booked at least one day in advance. A replacement bus serves the riverside stop while the bridge is being repaired. Contactless bank cards are accepted on buses but not on the heritage tram. The first Sunday service leaves Central Station at 8:10. A folded pushchair may be taken on board without an extra charge. The operator posts service changes on noticeboards and its website. Refund requests for unused weekly passes must be made before the pass begins.

passages.title: Using the Harbour Street library
passages.content:
Harbour Street library offers study space, digital access, and community activities. The following notice describes services available to members this year.

The reading room is open until 8 p.m. on Tuesday and Thursday. Members may borrow up to eight books at one time. Books are loaned for three weeks and can be renewed online once. The computer area requires a booking during school holidays. A quiet study room can be reserved in one-hour blocks. The weekly conversation group meets on Wednesday mornings. Large-print books are kept on the shelves beside the front desk. A replacement card costs two pounds. Children’s story time is intended for ages three to seven. The library accepts book donations only after staff have checked their condition. Printing is charged by the page, while scanning is free. The local history collection may be used inside the building but not borrowed. Members can ask staff to request a title from another branch.

passages.title: A community garden project
passages.content:
The fictional Eastbank Garden welcomes residents who want to grow food and improve a shared outdoor space. Its organisers explain how plots, tools, and volunteer sessions work.

New members attend a short orientation before receiving a plot. Each family plot measures four metres by two metres. Watering is restricted to early morning during dry-weather notices. The tool shed is opened by the volunteer coordinator on Saturdays. Organic waste is placed in the marked bays behind the greenhouse. Members label shared seedlings with the plant name and sowing date. Children must remain with an adult near the pond. The monthly work session takes place on the first Sunday. A small number of raised beds are reserved for residents with limited mobility. The garden does not permit chemical weedkiller on shared paths. Members may sell surplus produce only at the autumn open day. The greenhouse key is signed out at the community centre. The committee reviews plot use at the end of each growing season.
